title: Election Findings · documented survey and Census observations
methodology: 2024 and prior-election published survey analyses, ACS 2024 foreign-born state estimates. Do not treat aggregated people as individual votes.

sources.title: CIRCLE 2024 Youth Turnout, revised April 2025
sources.note: 2024 estimated from voter files in 40 states; older estimates from CIRCLE.

sources.title: CIRCLE / AP VoteCast Youth Vote in 2024
sources.note: AP VoteCast survey youth voter preference and issue priorities; uncertainty around percentages.

sources.title: Pew Research Center Validated Voters (2016, 2020, 2024)
sources.note: Presidential vote choice by age, race and ethnicity, and naturalized citizenship. Turnout is validated, and vote choice is self-reported.

sources.title: Pew 2024 validated-voter report
sources.note: Voter retention and participation. 2020 nonvoters who turned out in 2024.

sources.title: CRS report R48940, 2024 ACS 1-year DP02
sources.note: All 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico; foreign-born residents, including noncitizens; 90% MOEs.

warnings: Do not equate foreign-born population with voting electorate. Many foreign-born residents are not US citizens.
Do not equate ethnicity, immigrant status and naturalized status.
CIRCLE VoteCast and Pew validated-voter estimates use different survey methods; never pool counts or treat them as a single panel.
Age 18-29 at different elections is not a fixed Gen Z birth cohort.
Gen Z issue associations are not causal evidence of individuals deciding their votes.
The source observations cover through 2024 for these surveys, not 2026.
